PROBLEM (verified): a knowledge item's `leak_terms` entry does NOT block narration unless the same phrase is also one of the item's aliases or a multi-word `must_convey` phrase. The narration check builds `known_terms` from `indexes.audience_to_known_terms` and then keeps only those that are also keys of `indexes.leak_term_to_knowledge`, so `leak_terms` can only narrow, never add. The grounding guide promises that `leak_terms` "names the phrases narration must guard before the item is earned". In the continuity-initiative story, 3 of 70 entries are silently inert: item k_sl_1a_b_r0's 'taped beneath the drawer', 'taped under the drawer', 'taped to the drawer'. The owner decided to make `leak_terms` authoritative.

BUILD:
1. Make the guarded set the multi-word keys of `indexes.leak_term_to_knowledge` (case-folded), in BOTH places that build it: `NarrationSafetyValidator.validate` in narration_safety.py and `_validate_narration_term_traps` in loader.py. Put the rule in one small shared helper (for example a function next to `_compile_knowledge_indexes` in loader.py, or a property computed from the indexes) so the two sites cannot drift apart. Keep the multi-word rule (`len(term.split()) > 1`): single-word leak terms stay unenforced by design. Items WITHOUT `leak_terms` (None) must behave exactly as before: their aliases and multi-word must_convey phrases are already in the leak index.
2. The rest of the leak check (earned items, `earned_protected_terms`, owners, handoff text) stays as is. The new guarded phrases must be allowed on the turn their item is earned, as every other leak term already is.
3. If `_validate_narration_term_traps` now fails to load the continuity-initiative story because scene authored prose contains one of the newly guarded phrases, STOP and describe exactly which scene, phrase and text in the notes; do not edit story data and do not weaken the validator.
4. docs/markdown-story-authoring.md: replace the leak_terms paragraph so it says what is now true, in plain words: every multi-word phrase listed in `leak_terms` is blocked from narration before the item is earned; single-word entries are not enforced; absent means the old behaviour (aliases plus multi-word must_convey phrases); an empty list means the item has no guarded vocabulary. The text 'complete vocabulary that may be blocked' must be gone.

(the earning action; see k_sl_1a_b_r0's earn_when and action_evidence in knowledge.yaml). Use the engine path like tests/test_leak_terms.py (RuntimeEngine with a scripted provider and RuntimeState.bootstrap) or the NarrationSafetyValidator pattern; whichever lets the earn actually register. If acceptance on the earning turn does NOT hold, report it in the notes with the exact error and do not weaken the test.
- test_every_multiword_leak_term_in_the_story_is_enforced: for every story package under data/stories, every multi-word entry of every item's `leak_terms` is a member of the guarded set the validator now uses.
